newsitem.title: INDIA: India Hind Lever 96 net seen up 40 pct - analysts.
newsitem.headline: India Hind Lever 96 net seen up 40 pct - analysts.

text.p: Detergents and personal products giant Hindustan Lever Ltd, boosted by increased demand in rural India, is expected to post a 40 percent rise in net profit in calendar 1996, analysts said on Thursday.

According to a Reuter poll of 14 leading securities houses released on Tuesday, the company's net profit is projected to rise by 43 percent to an average 3.42 billion rupees, while sales are seen up by 35 percent to 45.74 billion this year.
"The company's strategy is not to increase prices and to go for smaller package sizes for its products," said analyst Sandeep Bhatia of UBS securities on Thursday.
Bhatia said HLL had passed on to customers the benefits it received from excise relief on its products.
India's two federal governments had in the past three years lowered excise duties on consumer products, including soaps and personal products, under a liberalised economic programme.
HLL, a subsidiary of the Anglo-Dutch conglomerate Unilever Plc, is a market leader in some brands of soaps, detergents and personal products. Unilever holds a 51 percent stake in the Indian company.
Bhatia said the company's soap segment, stagnant last year, began picking up this year with an anticipated growth of 8.0 percent. Detergents were expected to post 15 percent growth in 1996, he said.
Bhatia said a surge in demand for consumer products in rural India in the wake of widespread monsoon rains could further help Hindustan Lever's performance in the current year.
India is a predominently agricultural country, where a satisfactory monsoon normally leads to a good harvest of crops and higher incomes in rural areas.
"Personal products continue to be the driving factor for the company's growth," said analyst Ranjani Venkatesan at securities firm HG Asia.
Venkatesan said the company's proposed new launches of personal products also could help improve its performance.
"Marketing costs will be high, but it will have to live with them," she said. "The margins cannot change very much."
Venkatesan said fiscal budgets had been favourable to the company, but distribution costs had gone up due to higher freight charges.
"The high growth might not be sustainable," she said.
Analysts project a bigger role for the company in the near future.
HLL is expected to emerge as India's largest food and consumer products firm with the planned merger of Brooke Bond Lipton India Ltd, another Unilever subsidiary in India, by December.
